<reason>Both sides were disciplined, closed-book, and free of fake precision, and both progressed rather than repeated. PRO built the cleaner decision rule and stuck to it: if the firm captures output it would otherwise pay for, it is a job; if the intern is genuinely being taught, the motion's own carve-out applies. That dilemma forced CON to defend the grey middle explicitly, and CON's honest concession that such placements "only make sense if cash is not also required" was converted by PRO into the debate's most damaging frame — a business model whose viability depends on a family paying the intern's living costs. PRO also weighed quality against volume memorably ("a hundred chances... is zero, printed a hundred times") and conceded deletion openly rather than dodging, which made its equity comparison credible. CON's best live routes — deletion rather than conversion, administrability of "genuinely educational," and privilege migrating off the books — were real and pressed effectively; the counter that PRO's non-substitution test swallows the campaign office was the sharpest hit on PRO's carve-out. But CON never answered why the grey middle should be unpaid rather than paid beyond "firms won't," which is exactly the subsidy PRO indicted, and its "privilege goes off the books" claim stayed largely asserted against PRO's plausible reply that favours do not scale to an entire junior pipeline. CON's late "short, local, home-based unpaid slots" point was its best equity rejoinder but arrived in Rebuttal 2/closing with limited development. PRO answered the tougher pressure more directly; CON's "an internship is not a hire" answer to the minimum-wage parity question was coherent but thin.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's exploitation of CON's own line — that the placement "only makes sense if cash is not also required" — reframing it as a wage subsidy funded by family wealth rather than a rung. CON's reply (attach support to the host, restriction leaves nothing to fund) blunted it partially but never removed the sting.</best_rebuttal>
